title: Stable Baseline And Isolated Server Development
summary: Keep the current development line versioned independently from its compatibility baseline, and qualify Core, Observer, Server, and portable delivery as separate components.
policyScope: Development metadata describes source identities and isolation policy. It is not proof that a release, installation, or deployment has been qualified.

stableLane.maintenance: The compatibility baseline identifies contract provenance only. It does not qualify current public source or delivery.

artifactRetention.policy: Generated build outputs and measurements are disposable unless explicitly retained by a separate reviewed process.

localStableScope.core: Local offline Core and Observer are independently versioned.
localStableScope.server: The Server is optional and separately versioned.
localStableScope.boundary: No consumer cutover or installed-service claim is made here.

identityDirectory.boundary: Account binding and authorization contracts are separate from a source-only Core release.

releaseCandidate.qualification: A candidate requires the complete closure defined by shin-server-release-closure-v1.

developmentLane.contractBaselinePolicy: Historical compatibility baseline identity only; it is not current release evidence.
developmentLane.generatorTransitionPolicy: Snapshot compatibility is checked by generator identity. An incompatible snapshot requires an explicit rebuild; no implicit migration is performed.
developmentLane.currentScope: The public source contains independently versioned Core, Observer, and Server components. This profile declares source and contract scope only.
developmentLane.documentation: Keep component versions and generator identities in their declared source files and contracts.
developmentLane.candidateTool: Build into an explicit development output directory and compare each binary version with its source version file.

isolatedResources.builds: Use distinct build directories for Core, Observer, and Server.
isolatedResources.indexes: Generated indexes and reports use explicit external destinations.
isolatedResources.profiles: The public profile registry is explicit and checked into the source distribution.
isolatedResources.postgresql: A database is required only for Server runtime/integration work and must be disposable for tests.
isolatedResources.artifactsAndState: Keep test state separate from source and from any installed service.
isolatedResources.listeners: Bind test services to explicitly selected local endpoints.
isolatedResources.skills: Agent adapters are optional and do not alter Core runtime dependencies.
isolatedResources.makeTargets: Inspect target outputs before invoking a target that writes files.
isolatedResources.environment: Pass development configuration per process; do not alter global user settings.

branchRules.normalWork: Development and stable compatibility identities remain separate.
branchRules.backport: Backports require an independently reviewed and tested change.
branchRules.sync: Do not rewrite unrelated source or release history.
branchRules.remote: Publishing source is a separate owner action.
branchRules.consumerOwnership: Public contracts do not grant permission to modify external projects.

verificationLayers.runtime: Run the component checks required by the release closure.
verificationLayers.comparison: Compare only equivalent source, profile, generator, and limits.
verificationLayers.corpus: Synthetic fixtures and project-specific evidence are separate scopes.
verificationLayers.network: Network delivery and deployed service checks require separate evidence.

requirements: All required component and package gates pass on exact release inputs.
Compatibility is checked for source, schema, and generator identities.
Deployment and data migration are separately reviewed.
cutover.procedure: Publish a validated artifact and explicitly select the compatible route.
cutover.rollback: Retain a known compatible artifact and state recovery procedure.
cutover.compatibilityBoundary: Parallel component delivery does not imply compatibility with every historical data, protocol, or index format.
